A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Behavior-dLDS study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, comparisons with CLDS and PSID, and b-dLDS analyses of zebrafish hindbrain recordings in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds TaskRNN experiments, model comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies, and quantitative zebrafish asymmetry analyses.

M1.justification: v2 introduces the experimental b-dLDS-x variant, moving the behavioral readout and associated reconstruction objective from dynamics coefficients c to latent states x. The central b-dLDS architecture and inference procedure remain; Frobenius regularization and step-size rescaling were already present in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on delayanti task-trained RNN activations, with processing, memory, and response phases and 23 input/output behavior traces (Figure 4). This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained two-system simulations and zebrafish recording. The revised 14,000-neuron wording does not establish new zebrafish coverage: Appendix B retains the original recording and preprocessing counts.

E2.justification: The CLDS and PSID comparisons remain. v2 adds explicit zebrafish comparisons against unsupervised dLDS with post hoc behavior correlations and b-dLDS-x, including regularized and separately optimized variants (Table 3). b-dLDS-x also provides the comparator in the new TaskRNN experiment.

E3.justification: New protocols include fitting TaskRNN models on 64 of 80 trials, inference on all 80, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, and 500-iteration final fits (Appendix B.4.2). v2 also introduces matched-size zebrafish controls, 500-iteration sensitivity sweeps, and interpretability/asymmetry metrics. The retained simulation and zebrafish parameter tables largely preserve v1's settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds ablations of the Psi penalty and step-size rescaling (Supplementary Figure 5), behavior-supervision and latent-state-readout comparisons (Table 3), TaskRNN regularization sweeps (Table 1), and model-size/regularization sensitivity studies (Supplementary Figure 11, Table 8). New asymmetry analyses examine imaging-related baselines. These directly test components and failure conditions previously receiving little experimental scrutiny.

E5.justification: v2 adds baseline-asymmetry t-tests, reporting p<0.04 and p<0.001, and descriptive standard deviations in Table 2. It also documents three-seed TaskRNN runs and provides seedwise results and averages for new zebrafish comparisons and sensitivity sweeps. The original ten-seed CLDS comparison is retained; an increase in its run count is not reported.

E6.justification: New results include TaskRNN behavior R² of 0.99 versus 0.95 for b-dLDS and b-dLDS-x, extensive variant/sensitivity results, and six of 25 operators exceeding the 17% asymmetry baseline. The single-behavior zebrafish fit is replaced: v1 Figure 4 reports R²=0.90, whereas v2 Figure 5 reports neural R²=0.91 with different learned operators. Retained appendix displays also change operator 23's Psi value from 0.59 to 0.44 and operator 24's behavior R² from 0.22 to 0.11.

T1.justification: Equations 12–13 correct the differentiation variable from D to Psi, and Equation 13 places the Frobenius penalty inside the differentiated objective and adds an explicit update expansion. These are mathematical corrections beyond typesetting. Appendix A's connectivity derivation and assumptions remain unchanged, and no identifiability theorem is added.

C1.justification: Alongside the retained claims of separating behavior-related dynamics and scaling to large neural recordings, v2 adds prominent claims of interpretability advantages over latent-state readouts and post hoc dLDS analysis. The abstract and introduction also elevate previously unreported hindbrain asymmetry into a principal biological contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets comparable reconstruction with sparser behavioral mappings as support for dynamics-based readouts, develops a biological interpretation of hindbrain asymmetry, and discusses possible imaging artifacts. It explicitly limits the CLDS comparison's scope and acknowledges that robustness does not guarantee a unique identifiable decomposition. The original explicit nonstationarity interpretation of trial-type segmentation is softened.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed settings for the added model comparisons and TaskRNN experiments, optimization budgets, trial-type definitions, and expanded model-selection guidance. Table 3 adds runtime and memory estimates with measurement caveats. New availability statements promise zebrafish data upon request and simulation data/code upon publication; they do not establish an existing public release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through zebrafish laterality literature supporting its new hindbrain-asymmetry claim, Driscoll et al. (2024) for TaskRNN, and dictionary-learning identifiability work by Wu et al., Hu and Huang, and Cohen and Gillis. The original CLDS, PSID, and dLDS positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The six-section main-text organization and much of the existing prose remain. v2 refines state-versus-dynamics explanations, rewrites the conclusion, reorganizes appendix subsections, and replaces acknowledgments with availability sections and an impact statement. Editorial changes are concentrated around the larger scientific additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds the TaskRNN Figure 4, Supplementary Figures 5 and 11, and six tables covering comparisons, asymmetry, settings, and sensitivity. It replaces the single-behavior zebrafish visualizations, revises Figure 3's labels, and reformats parameter tables with row separators. Original Tables 1–2 become Tables 5 and 7, while several simulation figures remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps in v1 through comparisons within the dLDS family, the TaskRNN experiment, component ablations, and sensitivity studies (Figure 4, Table 3, Supplementary Figures 5 and 11). These substantially strengthen evidence for the central modeling choice and expose failure conditions. Detailed settings and explicit identifiability limitations improve transparency. The new asymmetry claim remains based on one fish, and resource estimates are acknowledged as rough, but these limitations do not outweigh the methodological validation gains.
